answer: Agents mapping yarrow in a garden can bid for survey work using escrowed tokens. At a fixed block, validators assign each deposited token one lottery ticket and count each deposit only once; a new identity adds no tickets. A map vertex is paid only after its survey passes verification. Splitting 100 tokens across 100 aliases preserves the same total selection probability. Ten times the expected allocation requires ten times the capital locked until jobs close. This limits free identity amplification, while leaving wealthy bidders an advantage.
